tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Oct 29 it ran through self-learning, pruning, Anthropic's Nov 2 provable-inference update and knowledge editing to Nov 10-13 work on what eval scores measure and when a model should abstain or ask for clarification.
whats_new: Nov 16: TRIAGE-CPG compares LLMs deciding under a budget whether to clear, flag or escalate unknown binaries, and dhAIBench benchmarks LLMs for linguistic annotation under documented conditions.
why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the recent run converges on a production question: when a model should answer, ask, abstain or escalate, and how to measure that decision rather than raw accuracy.

beats.headline: Keeping models current: RL-driven self-learning beyond plain RAG
beats.summary: Opens the window with knowledge acquisition coupled to reasoning in unfamiliar domains.

beats.headline: Efficiency work: extreme-sparsity pruning and an early-stopping audit for reasoning models
beats.summary: A text-to-SQL architecture survey lands the same day.

beats.headline: Anthropic reports progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference
beats.summary: The thread's only lab-published item: cryptographic proofs applied to LLM inference.

beats.headline: Updating what models know: answerability drift, multimodal unlearning and lifelong knowledge editing
beats.summary: Also here: an LLM choosing federated aggregation rules without training.

beats.headline: Judgment under scrutiny: rising rater standards on Chatbot Arena, framing effects and personality benchmarks
beats.summary: These days also bring an LLM AutoML searcher, physics-guided fault diagnosis, a training-simulation benchmark and a cognitive account of learning by thinking.

beats.headline: What do scores measure? ShadowBench and a corrupted-input study probe shortcuts behind passing evals
beats.summary: One tests recall without explicit entity names; the other asks whether LLMs pass NLI on noun-stripped or shuffled inputs.

beats.headline: Knowing when not to answer: black-box uncertainty and an interactive ambiguity-resolution eval
beats.summary: One splits prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps via API calls only; the other scores when a model should ask versus assume. A tabular anomaly-detection paper lands the same day.

beats.headline: Applied decisions: budgeted malware triage, annotation benchmarking and a survey of LLMs for AI infrastructure
beats.summary: The newest items move from model internals to LLMs making operational calls under cost and documentation constraints.

open_questions: Does TRIAGE-CPG report which models escalate too rarely or too often under a fixed analysis budget?
Does the ensemble-of-ensembles method report how many model calls per prompt it needs, and how that compares with deep ensembles?
Does the ambiguity-resolution eval show models asking for clarification at the right rate, or defaulting to assumptions?
Do published unlearning or knowledge-editing methods still pass when probed without explicit entity names, as ShadowBench suggests they may not?
Do Chatbot Arena or other human-preference leaderboards adjust rankings for the rater drift the Nov 10 study describes?
Does Anthropic publish proving cost or latency figures for zkSNARK-based provable inference?
take_for_builders: Score your agent's answer/ask/abstain/escalate decisions as a separate eval with perturbed controls (renamed entities, shuffled inputs), and measure the per-request call cost of any uncertainty method before wiring it into routing.
